fixes.explanation: That's the order, friend: "Gather up your belongings from this land, you who live under siege." (Jeremiah 10:17) Nobody is told to fight or to build. They're told to pack. I think that's a lot to take in when you're living under siege.

Close, baker, but the gates aren't in this verse. What it says is "Gather up your belongings from this land, you who live under siege." (Jeremiah 10:17) The order is to pack, and that's all it says. Nothing about the gates is in the line.
Wouldn't that be nice? The verse doesn't say that, though. The speaker says, "This is truly my sickness, and I must bear it." (Jeremiah 10:19) The word there is bear.

Flock it is. "…they have not prospered, and all their flock is scattered." (Jeremiah 10:21) The shepherds don't seek the LORD, and the flock they were supposed to look after is scattered. That's a shepherd's worst day.

Oh, friend, no. The text says the commotion "…will make the cities of Judah a desolation, a haunt for jackals." (Jeremiah 10:22) Full and thriving is the opposite of what's said. Desolation and jackals do not sound thriving to me.
Right, no thriving here. The commotion "…will make the cities of Judah a desolation, a haunt for jackals." (Jeremiah 10:22) Desolation is the word. Jackals are the ones who haunt those cities.

That's the word. The prayer says, "Correct me, O LORD, but only with justice—not in Your anger, or You will bring me to nothing." (Jeremiah 10:24) The prayer asks for correction with justice, and nothing is where anger would lead. I think that's a careful way to ask.
